author: Codex: focused Authority–Liberty reassessment
changeNote: Owner-authorised bank 3.0.0 revision. Reassessed authority-liberty-01, authority-liberty-02, authority-liberty-03, authority-liberty-04, authority-liberty-07, authority-liberty-08, authority-liberty-11, authority-liberty-12, authority-liberty-13 in the retained subject period; four unchanged-wording claims move within the axis and five claims have new mechanisms. All other 231 answer objects and fourteen other axes are preserved verbatim from revision 3. Retained dossiers, logged source-retrieval passages and specifically recorded supplementary research supply context. New exact responses/intensities are conservatively inferred; this is not a fresh re-verification of every earlier citation or a comprehensive new assessment of later developments. Scoring, weights, axis definitions, images, catalogue exclusions and religion supplements are preserved. No target placement or political-label adjustment is applied.

metadata.name: Joh Bjelke-Petersen
metadata.description: Queensland premier from 1968 to 1987, leading the Country/National Party. His government promoted resource and tourism development, resisted federal intervention and restricted political protest.
metadata.scope: Documented public positions and governing conduct during his Queensland premiership, including the 1987 federal campaign. National and modern hypothetical questions are explicitly inferred; this is neither a profile of all Queenslanders nor a claim he submitted the quiz.

axes.brief:
Regular elections coexisted with unequal electoral conditions and concentrated executive control. Assess actual conduct alongside his constitutional electoral participation.
Focused six-question reassessment: Party-selected premiership and strong executive control operated amid unequal electoral conditions. Technical government functions are assessed separately from political domination; direct binding national lawmaking is a modern extrapolation from a state-level career.
axes.counterEvidence:
He did not replace elections with military or expert rule; parliament and courts continued to operate and his party eventually removed him.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Party-selected premiership and strong executive control operated amid unequal electoral conditions. Technical government functions are assessed separately from political domination; direct binding national lawmaking is a modern extrapolation from a state-level career.

review.notes: Reviewed all nine revised records under literal mechanisms and the retained period, including direction, counter-evidence, institutional fit, response intensity, source relevance and each conditional Neutral. New educated-assumption IDs: authority-liberty-01, authority-liberty-02, authority-liberty-03, authority-liberty-04, authority-liberty-07, authority-liberty-08, authority-liberty-11, authority-liberty-12, authority-liberty-13. The retained period’s protest suppression, police power and moral regulation favour broad control. Precise bulk records and identity duties are historical estimates, not independently retrieved universal rules. Civil institutions and ordinary lawful organisations qualify intensity rather than supporting blanket freedom or total repression. Unchanged 231 objects and all other axes are preserved. Retrieval access alone does not establish evidence accuracy; retained source limitations and unavailable pages remain disclosed. Similarity decisions follow the complete batch, without adjusting answers to create separation.
